evidence_basis.originality_note: All learner contexts, wording, numerical values and figure geometry are original. Official evidence supplies only assessment demand patterns.

question_set_contract.dependency_contract: Exactly two questions use controlled prior learning: q01 directly retrieves couple torque and q07 combines couple torque with the principle of moments.
question_set_contract.difficulty_progression: prior retrieval, controlled definition, directional diagnosis, strategic point choice, equation diagnosis, multi-force application, then a multipart mixed application

questions.prompt: A mechanic applies a couple using two equal 18 N forces whose parallel lines of action are 0.24 m apart. Calculate the torque of the couple.
Write the complete principle of moments, including the condition under which it applies.
Which statement is required by the principle of moments?

options.A: Clockwise and anticlockwise moments are equal even while angular speed changes.
options.B: For rotational equilibrium, clockwise and anticlockwise moment totals are equal about the same point.
options.C: The largest clockwise force equals the largest anticlockwise force.
options.D: Clockwise moments about one point equal anticlockwise moments about a different point.

questions.prompt: A horizontal beam is attached to a wall by a hinge at H. The hinge force is unknown. Which point is the most useful point about which to take moments when finding another force on the beam?

options.A: The centre of the beam, because every force then has the same distance
options.B: The point where the other unknown force acts, because every other moment becomes zero
options.C: H, because the hinge force has zero perpendicular distance from H
options.D: Any point away from H, because the hinge force is then excluded

questions.prompt: A light bar is pivoted at P. A 12 N downward force acts 0.50 m to the left of P. A downward force F acts 0.35 m to the right. Which equation represents rotational equilibrium?

A uniform horizontal display arm of length 4.5 m is hinged to a wall at H. Its weight is 360 N. A 150 N lamp hangs 3.6 m from H. An upward vertical support force S acts at the far end. The arm is in rotational equilibrium.

A 50 N downward tool box is 0.35 m to the right of P. A downward counterweight force W is applied 0.50 m to the left of P. The platform is in rotational equilibrium.
